html:
The Zayyanid kingdom of Tlemcen ruled western and central Algeria from 1235 to 1556. It is shown here in 1492 and 1500, in its last century. Its earlier years are on the page Abd al-Wadids of Tlemcen.

Tlemcen was a city of scholars, mosques and merchants, and a terminus of the trans-Saharan trade. Genoese, Venetian and Catalan traders came to its ports. But the kingdom was weak, often a vassal of the Hafsids or the Moroccan sultans.

After Spain finished off Granada in 1492, it carried the war into Africa and took Oran in 1509. Zayyanid princes became Spanish clients. At the same time Ottoman corsairs led by the Barbarossa brothers set up in Algiers. Squeezed between Spain and the Ottomans, the kingdom ended when the Ottomans took Tlemcen in 1556.
